erroneous

ih-ROH-nee-us -- stress on the second syllable, ROH. · adjective

What It Means

Erroneous is wrong -- containing or based on an error, usually an honest one.

The weather service retracted its erroneous forecast after the promised 'sunny weekend' arrived as three days of rain.

Worked Example

The scoreboard operator posts the wrong total late in the game, and both teams spend the entire final minute playing as if the score were tied when it never was.

The posted score was erroneous -- simply wrong -- and every decision built on it inherited the mistake. A score sheet is only one home for erroneous marks. Information that is incorrect turns up in reports, forecasts, and charges too, and erroneous usually points to honest error rather than deceit.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

incorrect: Incorrect is the plain schoolroom word for not right -- an incorrect answer gets marked with an X and that is the end of it. Erroneous is the formal word for wrong information out in the world -- an erroneous report or forecast -- and it hints the error will mislead whoever relies on it.

mistaken: Mistaken points at the person or belief that got something wrong -- a mistaken impression, an honest error of memory or judgment. Erroneous points at the information itself: an erroneous figure, report, or charge. People and beliefs are mistaken; the data they produce is erroneous.

faulty: Faulty means built with a defect, so the thing fails when used -- faulty wiring, faulty reasoning, a faulty scale. Erroneous means the content itself is wrong. A faulty method is broken in how it works; an erroneous answer is simply wrong in what it says.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

accurate: correct in every detail

correct: free from error

Where it sits · how far from the truth it lands — inaccurate → erroneous → false

inaccurate vs. erroneous: Inaccurate is gentler than erroneous -- an inaccurate measurement is somewhat off the mark, while an erroneous one is flatly, plainly wrong.

false vs. erroneous: False can cut deeper than erroneous: an erroneous statement is wrong by honest mistake, while calling it false leaves room for something darker -- untrue through and through, perhaps even deliberately so.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — erron

Root — erron: a wanderer (from Latin erro, erronis, 'a wanderer, vagabond', built on errare 'to wander' -- the same root as error and erratic)

Suffix — -eous

Suffix — -eous: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Erron ('a wanderer', from Latin erro, erronis, built on errare 'to wander') + -eous ('full of') spell erroneous, using the -eous variant of this unit's suffix family. Something erroneous is 'full of wandering' -- a fact, label, or belief that has strayed off the path of truth and ended up in the wrong place entirely.

Use the root in a new word: erratic

Use the root in a new word: erratic: The old ferry's erratic timetable made it impossible to plan the morning crossing.

Root Check

Word Choice

Erroneous pairs with information words: an erroneous belief, report, assumption, conclusion, charge. It usually implies honest error -- someone got it wrong. When a falsehood is dressed up to deceive, this unit hands you spurious instead; erroneous is the mistake, spurious is the fake.
